title: The Evil Spirit Appears on An Unlucky Day
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro, Ran) and the local police inspector (Yokomizo, a procedural walk-on with no plot-load-bearing action) omitted by convention. Episode 416 has no subtitle file locally -- only 0415 (setup: the five 'curse' incidents, house tour, Sekiguchi's hanging) and 0417 (room searches, deduction, confession, shipwreck backstory) were available; 0417 opens with an in-show recap that bridges most of the missing middle, but any incremental clue-gathering unique to 416 could not be verified and is not represented here. Discrepancies vs. the old cases/ file: (1) the old file's label.murderer_id pointed only to the public chauffeur identity (s2/Masashi Watabiki); the transcript makes clear the actual hands-on strangler/heart-attack-inducer is Masashi's twin brother, presumed drowned in the shipwreck 13 years ago but secretly alive -- both twins are culpable (Masashi drove the alibi run and pre-planted his own fingerprints on the weapon and medicine bottle to frame an outsider) but the twin is the one performing the kills edges, so murderer_id now points to him, with Masashi modeled as an equally-guilty co-conspirator. (2) the old file's event e3 (Kunitomo's induced heart attack) was flagged is_crime_event:false, but the transcript is explicit this is the second of 'two murders' Conan sets out to solve -- corrected here. (3) old file's has_motive_against motive_type was left 'unspecified'; transcript grounds it concretely: Sekiguchi murdered his company's previous president 13 years ago and staged/caused the Kunitomo family cruiser's sinking to dispose of the body, drowning three household relatives (the twins' father, Namika's father, Akatsuka's wife) in the process, and Kunitomo himself later told police to call off the wreck search -- both twins target Sekiguchi and Kunitomo for this. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Nine known relatives across the three households vs. only eight birthday marks on Shigeko's calendar -- a shared mark hides a ninth person.
Watabiki's left-hand tree-rescue scar, visible when Namika recalls it, is absent minutes later when he borrows Ran's pen -- two physically identical, distinct people.
The handwriting in Watabiki's daily notebook looks consistent, but the circle drawn before each entry varies day to day -- two different hands wrote it.
Sekiguchi's watch is carved 'E' then 'N', but Akatsuka's compass shows N should come before E -- the carving is coordinates, not initials.
